about: The wording of each lead (what was read, in our words, and which open item it bears on). The address, time read and sha256 are taken from the run files by tools/perplexity-index.mjs, which writes leads.json.

pitch-semifinal-slot.title: The PITCH semi-final's slot was Wednesday 17:00 to 18:00, Centre Stage.
pitch-semifinal-slot.what: Web Summit's own session page for "PITCH semi-final" reads "November 11, 2026 • 5.00PM - 6.00PM Centre Stage" and carries no word of the storm or of a new slot. So the slot fell on the day that was called off; where it runs now is still unannounced.
bears_on: board c-pitch-original-slot (the conflict: Wednesday 17:00 or Thursday)
pitch-semifinal-slot.status: taken by incident.conductor@ as timeline row s-1111T0255 (03:02 UTC)

srpc-notice.title: Madeira's civil protection published its own notice on Charles.
srpc-notice.what: SRPC, IP-RAM's page "DEPRESSÃO CHARLES: MEDIDAS PREVENTIVAS", dated on the page "10 novembro 2026 3:27" (zone not stated): citing IPMA, worse weather in Madeira from Tuesday afternoon, the most critical rain between the end of the 10th and early morning of the 11th, south-westerly gusts up to 90 km/h and 130 km/h in the highlands, easing from Wednesday morning; expected effects listed (fallen trees, flash floods in urban areas). The service's home page also carries an English version.
bears_on: Madeira (the primary notice of the regional civil protection)
srpc-notice.status: already a fact in the record through incident.researcher@ (edge srpc-madeira-measures); this read confirms it

websummit-schedule-unchanged.title: Web Summit's schedule for Wednesday was still listed, unmarked, at 02:55 UTC.
websummit-schedule-unchanged.what: The organiser's schedule page for 11 November lists sessions from 9.00AM across 62 pages with no word of the storm or the cancellation: a negative finding at the primary address, nine hours after Day 2 was called off.
websummit-schedule-unchanged.status: taken by incident.conductor@ as timeline row s-1111T0255 (03:02 UTC)

ana-statement.title: ANA's own statement on the airports, with figures at 11:00.
ana-statement.what: ANA's newsroom, "Adverse weather conditions: update by airport – 11 November", dated 11 November 2026: at 11:00, Lisbon had 565 scheduled movements, 288 cancelled in advance by airlines, 45 operated and 22 further cancellations during the day; Madeira 80 scheduled, 20 cancelled in advance; Faro 62 and 14; Porto 214 and 12. ANA advises passengers to check with their airline before travelling. ANA's flights page (ana.pt, read 13:34) also carries its notice that adverse weather is affecting some flights. The engine returned the newsroom's address and said no statement was there; we followed it.
bears_on: decisions/entities/airport.json (open: ANA's statement read in the press only)

gov-despacho-page.title: The government's own page for the despacho, timed 13:11 on 10 November.
gov-despacho-page.what: portugal.gov.pt, Documentos, "Declaração de situação de alerta - despacho governamental publicado em Diário da República", 2026-11-10 às 13h11: the despacho declaring the alert from 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November for the whole mainland is published. Neither this page nor the government's news page of 10h33 names Web Summit: a negative finding at the primary address for the board's question on the government's advice.
bears_on: the timeline's 12:10 row on the alert situation
